audit_items.proof_trace: The liquidation path bypasses the EMA/spot deviation check entirely: `collaterals_usd_for_liquidation` (L1115) and `debts_value_usd_for_liquidation` (L1155) call `get_price` (EMA only, no deviation check), while `liquidate_calculate_seize_ctokens` (L1045-1046) uses `get_spot_price` (raw spot, no EMA comparison) to compute seized collateral. The non-liquidation path correctly applies the check via `get_price_with_check`, but the liquidation path has no guard, violating the property. The eligibility decision (EMA-based) and seizure amount calculation (spot-based) are internally inconsistent, meaning during high EMA-spot divergence the seized collateral can differ materially from what EMA-based protocol parameters intend.
audit_items.attack_scenario: During periods of naturally high EMA-spot price divergence (which coincide with volatile markets when liquidations are triggered), a liquidator calls `handle_liquidation`: eligibility is confirmed using EMA prices while the seized collateral amount is computed from the deviated spot price, causing borrowers to lose significantly more collateral than the EMA-based liquidation incentive parameters intend.
